page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on KVM virtualization. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 9T34 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance allocates 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading, backed by 128 GB of main system memory. This establishes a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The underlying processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, along with specialized instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware configurations exclude integrated local disk storage and discrete GPUs, meaning all persistent storage operations depend on remote network-attached volumes. Networking capabilities include a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps. Benchmark metrics indicate particularly strong compute performance in single-threaded tasks, where stress-ng single-core tests place the instance in the top 10% tier. Geekbench single-core (2,030) and multi-core (16,839) scores demonstrate upper-quartile capability, alongside PassMark memory (2,912.7) and cryptographic processing results. Conversely, multi-core throughput in stress-ng (49,860.38) and database execution scores fall within the middle 50% percentile range.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of ecs.g8ae.8xlarge aligns with dense general-purpose deployments where high single-thread clock rates and AVX-512 extensions reduce processing bottlenecks without the premium cost of dedicated memory-optimized or GPU hardware. Workloads suited for this server type include enterprise application servers, mid-tier in-memory caching platforms, CI/CD build environments, and web serving infrastructures requiring stable network throughput and balanced core-to-memory distribution.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 128 GB of RAM, it maintains a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and offering a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks highlight exceptional single-thread performance placing it in the top decile for single-core stress tests, supported by strong vector and cryptographic processing via AVX-512 and VAES instruction sets. Memory bandwidth and multi-core throughput perform solidly in average to strong tiers. The instance provides a balanced resource structure suitable for enterprise application hosting, CI/CD pipelines, container clusters, and general web workloads.
